subject: Clarify log deletion SLA and legal-hold options for VeriDoc Health (SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ)
messages:
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@veridoc-health.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: itsec@veridoc-health.com
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Log deletion SLA and legal-hold process (SOC 2 / SIG follow-up)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — VeriDoc is close to an internal decision but procurement needs clarification on our retention and deletion controls. Two specific asks from Legal/IT Sec:

1) For hosted Redwood API customers processing HCLS data, what are the standard retention windows for: (a) access logs (who called the API / metadata), (b) audit logs (configuration changes, auth events), and (c) request/response payloads (for debugging). We also need to know which of these are configurable per-customer.

2) Procurement requires a defined process for customer-initiated deletion and a documented legal-hold procedure. Can customers request a full deletion within 30 days of request? If a legal hold is required, how is that implemented operationally and what exceptions exist (e.g., SOC 2 evidence retention, incident investigations)?

We are preparing SIG/CAIQ answers and will flag anything that is ambiguous. Can you provide a short formal statement we can attach to our procurement questionnaire and share a couple of supporting artifacts (SOC 2 report, sample audit log export)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement is time-boxed for next week.

Best,
Sara
Sara Bennett
Head of Security & Compliance, VeriDoc Health
attachments: VeriDoc_SIG_Questions.xlsx (incoming)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@veridoc-health.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Log deletion SLA and legal-hold process (SOC 2 / SIG follow-up)

Sara — thanks for the note and the clear asks. High level answers below; looping in Neha (Security) and Monica (Customer Success) to confirm operational details and provide artifacts.

Summary (short):
- Standard hosted retention: access logs = 90 days, audit logs = 365 days, request/response payloads = 30 days by default.
- Configurability: For Dedicated and Private deployments, retention windows are configurable in the service contract / tenant settings. For Hosted, we can offer contract-level adjustments (e.g., 30-day access logs) but require a DPA/RPO addendum for anything outside standard windows.
- Deletion: Customers can request deletion of customer content and request/response payloads; typical turnaround is 30 calendar days for hosted accounts after validation. Audit logs and immutable SOC 2 evidence are protected — they cannot be deleted from our central compliance store without an approved exception and legal review.
- Legal hold: We support a legal-hold workflow: flag the tenant, suspend automatic deletion, preserve relevant evidence exports, and provide an agreed retention window. Legal holds require an authorized contact + signed request; operating the hold may be accompanied by a temporary export of logs to a customer-managed storage for investigations.

I will attach SOC 2 report and a small sample audit-log export in a follow-up. Neha / Monica — can you confirm the exact phrasing we should use for the procurement statement (one paragraph) and confirm whether we can offer a 30-day access-log window for Hosted with procurement-level approval?

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-05T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Log deletion SLA and legal-hold process (comments for VeriDoc)

Karthik / Monica — quick internal note before we send a formal response to VeriDoc. Key constraints and proposal:  

- Compliance constraints: Our SOC 2 implementation requires we retain immutable audit evidence for a minimum of 12 months for our control testing; that evidence is stored in an append-only compliance store and cannot be removed except under extraordinary legal directives. This is non-negotiable from an audit posture.

- Customer-facing logs vs. compliance evidence: We can differentiate between (A) customer-facing access logs and request payloads (which we can purge per customer request), and (B) internal audit evidence used for SOC 2 testing (control logs, change history snapshots). For (A) we can offer 30/60/90 day windows as part of the contract; for (B) minimum 365 days.

- Legal hold: Operationally we will: (1) freeze the tenant's deletion schedules, (2) produce an evidence export within 7 business days, (3) place a hold flag in the tenant metadata. Any purge of compliance evidence will require Legal + Security signoff and a ticket to the compliance team; expect 1-2 weeks for review.

- Alternative for VeriDoc (HCLS): If VeriDoc requires shorter living access logs but wants to keep SOC 2 alignment, we can offer: keep access/response payload retention at 30 days (hosted) and maintain an aggregated/hashed compliance digest for 365 days (no PII, for control verification). This preserves auditability without exposing full payloads.

I can draft the one-paragraph procurement-friendly statement. Monica — can CS confirm if we have recent examples where a customer requested 30-day access logs for Hosted and how we handled it?

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Hi Sara — following up with an agreed, procurement-ready statement and supporting notes below. Attaching: Redwood SOC 2 report (redwood-soc2-2025.pdf) and a small audit-log sample (example-audit-log-sample-2026-06.csv).

Procurement statement (one-paragraph, please attach to SIG/CAIQ):
"Redwood Inference maintains clear, configurable retention windows for customer data and logs. For our hosted API service the default retention windows are: access logs — 90 days; audit logs / SOC 2 evidence — 365 days; request/response payloads — 30 days. For Dedicated and Private deployments retention windows can be adjusted via contract. Customers may request deletion of customer content and transient request payloads; standard hosted deletions complete within 30 calendar days after validation. Audit logs and compliance evidence required for SOC 2 cannot be removed from Redwood's append-only compliance store without an approved legal exception. Redwood supports a documented legal-hold process: authorized customer contacts may request and sign a hold, we will suspend automatic deletion schedules and provide evidence exports; any removal of compliance artifacts requires Legal + Security approval and is executed under a documented exception."

Operational notes (short):
- We can offer contract-level adjustments to access-log and payload retention for Hosted customers after procurement review (rare, requires DPA addendum).
- For HCLS customers we recommend: 30-day request/response payloads + 365-day compliance digest (hashed/aggregated) to balance privacy and auditability.
- Turnaround: evidence exports for investigations — 7 business days; deletion confirmations — 30 calendar days.

Next steps: if VeriDoc wants the one-paragraph in a letterhead or a signed addendum, let me know and we can route to Legal for signature. Attached artifacts: redwood-soc2-2025.pdf, example-audit-log-sample-2026-06.csv.

Best,
Karthik
